A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SiLVR. Their main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VideoQA evaluations, knowledge-acquisition and temporal-grounding results, ablations, and appendix experiments including HourVideo.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds baseline comparisons, efficiency measurements and further ablations.

M1.justification: The default two-stage pipeline and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged; Adaptive Token Reduction is renamed Adaptive Context Reduction. Section 4.7 adds limited experimental adaptations: progressively shortening captions to 40/20/10 words, concatenating two captioners’ outputs, and incorporating non-uniform frame sampling.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same eight main benchmarks plus HourVideo, including knowledge acquisition and grounded QA. CGBench-Reasoning adds evaluation of an existing benchmark’s subset. ASR removal and sampling variants change experimental configurations within the retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluated comparators: Table 1 adds Gemini 2.5, Qwen-3-VL and Video-R1 models; Tables 3–4 introduce comparisons with VideoAgent, DrVideo, VideoTree and VCA. DeepSeek-V3 joins the eight-benchmark reasoning comparison in Table 2, although it already appeared in v1’s narrower LLM ablation.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation design with runtime measurements on VideoMME long without ASR, specified A6000 hardware, 32/768-frame configurations, and SiLVR-fast/best settings. It also adds ASR-removal controls, caption-word budgets, clustered sampling and evaluation on the CGBench reasoning subset. These supplement the retained original protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond v1’s existing ablations, v2 tests ASR removal across eight benchmarks, word-limit versus segment-count reduction, uniform versus clustered sampling, context-length effects, captioner ensembles and additional backbone models. These substantially expand examination of component contributions and tradeoffs. The qualitative examples were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The expanded results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: SiLVR’s Table 1 scores are retained, but the added Gemini 2.5 Pro result changes its Video-MMMU ranking: 82.7 versus 83.6. Substantial new entries include runtime/accuracy comparisons, ASR ablations, CGBench-Reasoning accuracy of 36.3 and GPT-5-backed VideoMME accuracy of 73.9. These represent additional comparisons and configurations. Table 2’s new reported general-benchmark gain of 3.8 disagrees with the 1.7 average calculated from its displayed rows.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions in Section 3.1 and the knowledge-acquisition formula in Equation 1 are retained. Neither version develops theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion remove Video-MMMU comprehension from the best-reported-performance claim, narrowing the headline benchmark list from five to four. The central claims about a modular, training-free language-based video reasoning framework remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of efficiency/accuracy tradeoffs, ASR benefits across domains, captioner ensembles, and why finer visual information can outweigh longer-context costs. The original module-dependence limitations and explanation of counting difficulties remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents hardware for the new efficiency experiment, CLIP/k-means sampling with 32 clusters, and adaptive caption-word limits. Appendix C’s existing implementation instructions remain largely unchanged. The explicit GitHub code-availability link is removed from the abstract and replaced with the project-page link; this does not establish that the code became unavailable.

R1.justification: Related work adds citations including Visual CoT, VideoEspresso, MOREVQA and VAMOS, with further VCA and context-length references. Positioning against agent-based pipelines is refined to emphasize single-pass reasoning and adaptive context reduction. The broader research positioning remains consistent.

P1.justification: Terminology changes from ATR to ACR, comparison passages are revised, and the experiment section gains agent-comparison, efficiency and qualitative subsections. Much of the introduction, method, limitations and technical appendix remains closely matched, so the language and narrative revision is limited.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column TMLR format, with extensively rearranged and expanded tables, including new size and context-length columns. v1’s appendix Figures 6–7 become main-text Figures 4–5 in v2; the other qualitative examples are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Previously missing agent/efficiency comparisons and targeted component controls make the contribution easier to assess, while narrowing the Video-MMMU headline claim improves alignment with Table 1. These benefits are tempered by reporting errors: Table 2’s new average gain conflicts with its rows, several best-model captions are stale, and Section 4.8 states 15 inches where the retained reasoning trace answers 9.4 inches. The net quality gain is therefore limited.
